newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cr Lyonnais advances on recovery hopes.
newsitem.headline: Cr Lyonnais advances on recovery hopes.

text.p: Shares in state-controlled Credit Lyonnais shot up on Monday on investor hopes that the French bank could be a recovery play.
"It seems to be the flavour of the month right now," said one analyst.

At 1128 GMT, the non-voting shares were up 5.71 percent at 207.30 francs on 78,033 shares traded. The shares, which make up around 20 percent of the bank's capital, have been rising steadily from a low of 94.55 francs touched last June.
Traders said the latest stimulus for the share's rise had come from a Wall Street Journal article on Monday.
The article quoted a couple of market players as saying the bank could replicate the turnaround success of some U.S. and Swedish banks to deliver rich returns for investors.
While some analysts were bullish on the stock, other analysts were more cautious.

"I have 230 francs as a 12-month horizon," said one analyst on Monday, who rated it a speculative share. "Even after it has got its act together, I'm not suggesting this will be a highly profitable bank."
Analysts took a divided view of the government's decision on Friday to delay delivering to the European Commission its already late bailout plan for the bank to the end of March.

Some believed that Brussels would demand the government accelerate the timetable for its privatisation. The government said on Friday it did not expect the bank to be ready for sale until the end of 1998 or the beginning of 1999.
Others said they saw the delay in presenting the plan as a bad sign. "It looks to me like it is back to the drawing board," one said.
